messages:
Incident Bot: P1 alert — Dedicated GPU pool 'dp-acme-usw2' reporting 100% GPU utilization for >5m, queue backlog rising. Affected tenant: AcmeCorp (dedicated pool). Autoscaler reports 'no capacity remaining'.
Li (oncall): Acked. Pulling logs and autoscaler state now.
Li (oncall): Quick check — is burst capacity enabled for this pool?
Sam W: Confirmed burst is ON for this pool but burst tokens are exhausted. Looks like tail of long batch jobs from AcmeCorp hit simultaneously.
Marta G: Do we have pre-warmed nodes for this pool? I think Dedicated pools are strict per-tenant unless burst to shared is allowed.
James (infra): dp-acme-usw2 is isolated; there's a config toggle allow_shared_burst=false for this tenant (security request). No pre-warms left in region.
Li (oncall): Impact check — which customers are failing requests? Any 5xx spikes or latency SLO misses?
Sam W: Metrics: 5xx from AcmeCorp spike from 0.1% to 12% in last 6m. Latency p95 increased from 120ms to 2.3s for their realtime routes. Other tenants on same host pool unaffected.
Li (oncall): Thanks. Prioritize containment and customer's traffic. Options: 1) Temporarily enable allow_shared_burst for this pool (violates customer isolation policy). 2) Enable manual capacity add (spin up extra dedicated nodes) — takes ~20-30m. 3) Ask customer to pause heavy batch jobs. 4) Route their realtime traffic to hosted fallback model (if allowed).
Priya (acct): I'm pinging AcmeCorp AM now. They have enterprise support but will need approval for any config that touches isolation. Sending contact.
Marta G: If we enable hosted fallback, what data residency / privacy implications? AcmeCorp signed VPC-only clause for some endpoints. Need to confirm which routes are allowed to failover.
James (infra): We can spin up 4 gpus in the dedicated pool w/ reserved capacity in the same region — provisioning estimate 18-25m. Hot path for realtime could be shifted to hosted variant for next ~30m; that requires toggling their routing policy.
Li (oncall): Action: 1) Priya -> confirm which API keys/routes can be failovered. 2) James -> start manual capacity add (provision extra nodes). 3) Sam/Marta -> prepare to enable hosted fallback if Priya confirms. 4) Ops Runbook Bot -> create incident channel and run checklist.
Ops Runbook Bot: Created #inc-1762104823-acme-dp-exhaustion and attached runbook 'dedicated_pool_exhaustion_v2'.
Priya (acct): AcmeCorp responding — they give permission to failover non-PHI realtime endpoints to hosted for up to 2 hours. They will not allow batch dataset ingestion to move.
Sam W: Ok, we can target realtime routes. Which route names? /v1/generate-stream and /v1/chat -> those are non-PHI for AcmeCorp.
Marta G: I'm prepping routing change. Need confirmation of token mapping and canary percent (start 10%).
Li (oncall): James, how's provisioning? ETA?
James (infra): Provision job kicked off: request id prov-9803. Logs:
```
> k8s apply -f dp-acme-scaleup-4.yaml
Scaling group request accepted; instance boot 2/4 complete
GPU drivers installing on node-1, node-2
```
Li (oncall): Start hosted fallback canary now at 10% for realtime routes. Sam, Marta — execute in console.
Sam W: Doing the canary. Console change:
```
route:update --tenant acmecorp --route /v1/generate-stream --fallback hosted --canary 10
```
Sam W: Canary live at 10%. Monitoring p95 and error rate for canary.
Li (oncall): Observing metrics... canary looks healthy at 10% — no errors, p95 ~150ms. Increase to 25% to relieve load.
Sam W: Increased to 25%.
Marta G: Noted. Informing security team but this is within allowed endpoints per Priya.
Priya (acct): AcmeCorp confirms canary is fine. They asked that we not change any batch ingest jobs.
Li (oncall): Autoscaler update — burst tokens report reset in 7m? Or are they exhausted until next billing window?
Sam W: Burst tokens are tied to reserved pool credits; they're exhausted and won't replenish until scheduled top-up. So cannot rely on burst.
James (infra): Nodes at 3/4 healthy. One node still initializing; GPU driver failed once, requeued. Working on logs. ETA full healthy 9m.
Li (oncall): Once nodes healthy, we can shift more traffic back to dedicated pool and reduce hosted fallback. Priority: minimize customer 5xx and keep data policy constraints.
Ops Runbook Bot: Reminder checklist: 'notify-customer', 'spin-up-dedicated', 'enable-fallback', 'log-change'. All marked in progress.
Sam W: Hosted fallback at 25% reduced 5xx to 6%. Good progress.
Marta G: After nodes healthy, plan: 1) shift realtime 50% back to dedicated, 2) monitor for 10m, 3) if stable, remove hosted fallback.
James (infra): Node-4 came up healthy. Full group shows 4/4. Rebalancing GPU pods now:
```
kubectl rollout restart ds/dp-acme-runtime -n dp-acme
```
James (infra): Pods redistributed; GPU usage dropping.
Li (oncall): Seeing p95 drop to 300ms and 5xx to 1.2% overall. Reduce hosted fallback to 10% while we monitor.
Sam W: Reduced hosted fallback to 10%.
Priya (acct): AcmeCorp appreciates fast response. They've paused non-critical batch jobs and will resume later.
Li (oncall): Continue to monitor for 20m. James, leave new capacity and follow up with infra to make the extra nodes part of future reserved capacity quote for AcmeCorp.
James (infra): Filing ticket to sales/finance to propose short-term reserve for the extra 4 GPUs and update autoscaler credits. ticket# RF-3421.
Ops Runbook Bot: Checklist updated: all mitigation steps complete, continuing monitoring.
Marta G: Summary for postmortem: root cause — simultaneous large batch launches plus exhausted burst tokens w/ isolation config disallowing shared burst. Mitigations: faster autoscale path (reduce provision time), clearer customer guidance on batch windows, option to pre-warm for heavy jobs, and options to relax isolation in emergency with customer opt-in.
Li (oncall): I'll create incident postmortem and tag eng-runtime, eng-infra, product, and acct. Assigning to Sam for timeline and James for infra action items.
Sam W: Got it. I'll draft timeline and paste logs.
James (infra): I'll add infra remediation and quota change request.
Li (oncall): Closing active mitigations. We'll keep thread open for postmortem notes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
